faq.question: Can I enroll as a complete beginner with no prior design background?
faq.answer: Yes. Creative Design Master starts from the ground up. Module 01 builds visual foundations, Gestalt principles, microtypography, and color theory before introducing professional software. No prior design degree or drawing expertise is required.

faq.question: What is the duration and weekly time commitment of this program?
faq.answer: The program spans 8 Months (32 Calendar Weeks) and includes exactly 320 Guided Instructional Hours (~10 hours per week of live mentored instruction). We recommend an additional 5–8 hours weekly for independent studio lab practice and case study building.

faq.question: How are the 320 guided instructional hours distributed across the course?
faq.answer: The 320 guided hours are distributed across 12 focused modules: Design Foundations (24h), Photoshop Compositing (32h), Illustrator Vector Art (36h), Brand Strategy (32h), Advertising Campaigns (24h), Editorial Design (20h), Packaging Design (16h), Figma UI/UX (28h), Responsive UI Systems (28h), Motion Graphics (24h), Generative AI Art Direction (28h), and Integrated Capstone (28h).

faq.question: How are Photoshop and Illustrator differentiated in this curriculum?
faq.answer: Adobe Photoshop is mastered for raster graphics, non-destructive photo manipulation, Frequency Separation retouching, perspective-matched compositing, and smart object mockups. Adobe Illustrator is mastered for precision vector mathematics, anchor point economy, geometric circular grid logos, iconography systems, and structural packaging dielines.

faq.question: What commercial branding and packaging skills will I build?
faq.answer: You will develop complete corporate identity systems (responsive logo suites, Pantone color governance, type hierarchies, Brand Manuals), structural folding carton dielines, label design, barcode integration, and prepress spot color separations for Spot UV varnish and Hot Foil stamping.

faq.question: Does this course cover digital product UI and UX design in Figma?
faq.answer: Yes. Modules 08 and 09 dedicate 56 guided hours to digital interface design. You will learn user research basics, information architecture, wireframing, the 8pt spatial grid, pure Auto-Layout 5.0, design tokens, Figma Variables (Light/Dark mode), and interactive Smart Animate prototyping.

faq.question: What motion graphics competencies are taught in After Effects?
faq.answer: Module 10 teaches the 12 principles of animation, custom Speed Graph velocity sculpting, vector shape layer operators (Trim Paths, Repeater), kinetic typography with text animators, 4-second commercial logo reveal stings, and exporting lightweight Lottie JSON animations for web developers.

faq.question: Which Generative AI tools are taught, and how are they integrated?
faq.answer: You will master Adobe Firefly, Photoshop Generative Fill/Expand, Illustrator Text to Vector/Recolor, Midjourney v6/v7, ChatGPT, and Google Gemini. AI is taught as an advanced art direction pipeline under strict human direction; raw unrefined AI outputs are never accepted as client deliverables.

faq.question: How are Adobe Firefly generative credits and usage managed?
faq.answer: Classroom projects utilize standard generative credits included with student Adobe Creative Cloud subscriptions. We explicitly teach credit budgeting, standard vs premium models, and fallback generation speeds so you can execute client projects efficiently without unexpected costs.

faq.question: Are software licenses included in the tuition fee?
faq.answer: No. Tuition covers instructional delivery, dedicated mentor reviews, portfolio evaluations, and career support. Students utilize affordable student/educational licenses for Adobe Creative Cloud (~₹1,500/mo) and Figma's 100% free verified Education Plan. On-campus students have full access to dedicated lab workstations.

faq.question: Do I need to pay for an expensive Midjourney subscription?
faq.answer: No. Advanced Midjourney art direction workflows are demonstrated live by faculty. Students can complete assignments using free trial credits, shared campus studio seats, or Adobe Firefly equivalents with zero mandatory subscription requirement or grading penalty.

faq.question: Will I work on real-world or simulated client briefs?
faq.answer: You will work on commercially authentic client briefs modeled directly after real startup, D2C, and corporate agency mandates. These briefs include explicit audience personas, commercial constraints, mandatory copy, and milestone deadlines.

faq.question: Will I own the editable source files for my portfolio projects?
faq.answer: Yes, 100%. You create, own, and retain all layered editable source files (.PSD, .AI, .INDD, .FIG, .AEP). These master source files serve as verifiable proof of your technical software competence during agency job interviews.

faq.question: What are the six canonical portfolio case studies I will build?
faq.answer: You will graduate with 6 major commercial case studies: 1. Complete Brand Identity System, 2. Integrated Advertising Campaign, 3. Packaging & Editorial Production, 4. Responsive Figma UI/UX Project, 5. Motion Brand Identity, and 6. Integrated AI-Assisted Creative Agency Capstone.

faq.question: What career roles will I qualify for upon graduation?
faq.answer: Graduates are qualified for roles such as Creative Designer, Graphic Designer, Brand Identity Designer, Visual Designer, Campaign Designer, Junior UI Designer, Creative Production Artist, and Junior Motion Designer. In accordance with truth-in-education standards, senior creative director roles require additional years of professional leadership.

faq.question: What is the commercial tuition fee for Creative Design Master?

faq.answer: Yes. In accordance with Indian tax regulations, statutory 18% GST (INR 11,682) applies, bringing the total gross fee to INR 76,582. An official tax invoice with GST breakdown is issued upon enrollment.

Brainstorming headline and CTA variations with ChatGPT and testing visual hooks

Dynamic page numbering (folios), running headers, section markers, and chapter prefixes
Baseline grid configuration: Snapping body copy to uniform baseline rhythm across spreads
Binding considerations: Creep compensation for saddle-stitch and spine width calculation for perfect bound books
lessons.why_it_matters: Manually applying page numbers or headers across a 48-page publication wastes hours and invites errors. Parent pages and baseline grids automate document consistency across hundreds of pages.
lessons.what_learner_does: Set up a 16-page editorial publication document with parent pages for covers, feature articles, and interview spreads; configure automatic folios and a global 12pt baseline grid.

lessons.lesson_title: Automated Editorial Typography, Styles & GREP Expressions

Advanced OpenType features: True small caps, discretionary ligatures, tabular figures, and fractions
Nested styles: Automatically formatting lead-in run-in heads and drop caps
GREP styles: Writing regular expressions to format dates, phone numbers, currency symbols, and acronyms automatically
Text frame options: Multi-column frames, first baseline offset, vertical justification, and baseline snapping

lessons.expected_outcome: A robust InDesign style library with cascading Paragraph, Character, and GREP styles formatting raw text instantly upon pasting.

Threaded text frames and primary text flows for multi-page manuscript import
Text wrap options: Bounding box, contour wrap around object clipping paths/alpha channels, and invert wrap
Designing editorial sidebars, callout boxes, pull quotes, author bios, and footnotes
Table design: Alternating row colors, cell padding, headers, and importing structured CSV/Excel data

lessons.what_learner_does: Design a dynamic 8-page feature article for an architecture or design publication; thread a 2,000-word text flow; wrap text around an extracted silhouette; insert pull quotes and styled data tables.
lessons.expected_outcome: A visually captivating 8-page editorial feature spread exhibiting harmonious visual pacing, zero text overset errors, and refined layout dynamics.
lessons.example: Wrapping multi-column body text tightly around the organic curve of an architectural building silhouette using Photoshop alpha channel clipping paths.

lessons.lesson_title: Preflight Auditing, Color Management & Print-Ready PDF Packaging
lessons.what_is_taught: Prepress quality assurance: Live Preflight panel configuration, link management, resolving missing fonts/links, CMYK color profiles, ink coverage (TAC <= 300%), packaging archives, and exporting certified PDF/X-1a and PDF/X-4 files.

Links panel management: Relinking modified assets, updating paths, and embedding vs linking best practices
Color management: Converting RGB assets to CMYK FOGRA39 / GRACoL, rich black rules, and total ink limit (TAC <= 300%)
Packaging publication archives: Collecting fonts, high-res linked images, and generating automated instruction reports
PDF export presets: Commercial print standards (PDF/X-1a vs PDF/X-4), crop marks, bleeds, and digital interactive PDF export

lessons.what_learner_does: Run a comprehensive preflight audit on a complete publication; fix 5 simulated errors (overset text, RGB image, missing font); package the document archive and export an ISO-compliant PDF/X-4.
lessons.expected_outcome: A fully packaged InDesign publication folder containing fonts, linked CMYK assets, and a certified print-ready PDF/X-4 with crop marks and 3mm bleeds.
lessons.example: Catching and resolving a hidden 3-line text overset overflow inside an article frame before sending the file to the commercial printer.

Packaging substrates: SBS paperboard, kraft, rigid boxes, flexible film pouches, and glass labels

lessons.what_is_taught: Foundational user experience concepts: UI vs UX, human-centered design thinking (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test), identifying user pain points, basic user research, personas, and competitive benchmarking.
subtopics: The spectrum of digital design: UI visual craft vs UX interaction architecture
The 5 stages of Design Thinking applied to digital product challenges
Conducting lightweight user research: User interviews, observation, and competitive benchmarking
Developing evidence-based User Personas and Empathy Maps
Mapping user journeys: Identifying emotional highs, lows, and high-friction drop-off points
lessons.why_it_matters: A beautiful user interface that solves the wrong problem will fail in the marketplace. Grounding visual design in user research ensures products deliver intuitive commercial utility.

lessons.lesson_title: Information Architecture, Sitemaps & User Flows

Building structural sitemaps and navigational trees in FigJam
Designing task flows and user flows with decision gates and error termination states
Navigational hierarchies: Tab bars, bottom navigation, hamburger drawers, and sticky headers
Content inventories: Auditing required content blocks prior to screen design

lessons.what_learner_does: Map the complete information architecture and screen-to-screen user flow for a digital healthcare or e-commerce platform in FigJam, accounting for happy paths and error states.

subtopics: Rapid thumbnail wireframing on paper: Exploring 10 screen layouts in 15 minutes
Building digital low-fidelity wireframes in Figma without visual styling distractions
The 8-point spatial grid system: Spacing, sizing, and padding in multiples of 8 (and 4 for micro-spacing)
Responsive layout column grids: 12-column desktop (1440px) and 4-column mobile (390px)
Visual hierarchy in UI: Guiding visual attention using scale, weight, and spatial grouping

lessons.lesson_title: UI Visual Polish, Accessibility & Interaction States
lessons.what_is_taught: Transforming wireframes into polished interfaces: UI typography scales, color psychology in UI, accessible contrast compliance (WCAG 2.1 AA), interaction states (default, hover, pressed, disabled), and form patterns.
subtopics: UI typography hierarchy: Establishing display, headline, body, label, and caption styles
Accessible color contrast: WCAG 2.1 AA standards (4.5:1 for body copy, 3:1 for large text and UI controls)

Interactive component states: Designing default, hover, focused, active, loading, and disabled states
Form design patterns: Floating labels, inline validation messages, input masks, and clear error recovery
lessons.why_it_matters: Low-contrast text and ambiguous buttons exclude users with visual impairments and cause severe usability failures. Accessible UI design is a legal and ethical commercial requirement.
lessons.what_learner_does: Apply high-fidelity visual styling to the wireframe screens; audit all text contrast against WCAG 2.1 AA; design all interactive states for form inputs and primary buttons.
lessons.expected_outcome: A high-fidelity 4-screen UI interface featuring WCAG-compliant color contrast, refined typography, and documented interactive states.

lessons.lesson_title: Auto-Layout Mastery & Responsive Constraints
lessons.what_is_taught: The engine of modern interface design: Auto-Layout 5.0 mechanics, direction (vertical, horizontal, wrap), independent padding, gap spacing, alignment, hug contents vs fill container, min/max constraints, and nested hierarchies.
subtopics: Auto-Layout fundamentals: Direction, independent padding (top, right, bottom, left), and gap between items
Resizing constraints: Hug Contents, Fixed Width/Height, and Fill Container mechanics
Min and Max dimensions: Enforcing minimum and maximum container widths to prevent broken layouts
Auto-Layout Wrap: Creating dynamic responsive chip filters and multi-row tag clouds
Nested auto-layout hierarchies: Combining vertical and horizontal frames to construct bulletproof responsive cards
lessons.why_it_matters: Static frame-based designs break the instant text content changes or viewport sizes shrink. Pure auto-layout ensures components flex and reflow dynamically like real browser code.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build a complex e-commerce product card containing an image, badges, ratings, variable-length title, pricing, and button, configured so resizing the card reflows all child elements flawlessly.

lessons.lesson_title: Design Tokens, Variables & Theming
lessons.what_is_taught: Foundations of design systems: Atomic Design methodology (Atoms, Molecules, Organisms), design token taxonomy (primitive vs semantic tokens), Figma Variables, and creating instantaneous Light/Dark mode themes.
subtopics: Atomic Design taxonomy: Categorizing UI elements into Atoms, Molecules, and Organisms
Design tokens: Primitive values (e.g. blue-500) vs semantic functional tokens (e.g. bg-primary, text-brand)
Typography styles: Configuring global text styles for Display, Title, Body, and Caption across viewport scales
Figma Variables: Setting up color variables, number variables (spacing/radius), and string variables
Creating Variable Modes: Configuring instant switching between Light Mode and Dark Mode across entire screens
lessons.why_it_matters: Hardcoding hex codes across hundreds of screens makes rebrands and dark mode implementations nightmare projects. Tokenized variables enable system-wide updates in seconds.
lessons.what_learner_does: Build a design token library in Figma containing color, spacing, radius, and typography tokens; configure Variable Modes and demonstrate instant Light-to-Dark theme switching on a dashboard card.
lessons.expected_outcome: A structured Figma Variable collection and a dashboard UI screen that flips between Light and Dark modes with zero manual recoloring.
lessons.example: Binding background frames to a semantic 'surface/container' token that resolves to #FFFFFF in Light Mode and #1E293B in Dark Mode.

lessons.lesson_title: Master Components, Variants & Component Properties

subtopics: Main Components vs Instances: Override hygiene, resetting overrides, and component detachment rules
Component Variants: Organizing multi-state components (Default, Hover, Active, Disabled, Loading)
Component Properties: Boolean properties to toggle icons, Text properties for instant copy editing
Instance Swap properties: Enabling one-click icon swapping from a centralized icon library
Building complex molecules: Form inputs with trailing icons, dropdown select menus, and modal dialogs
lessons.why_it_matters: Without component properties, design files become bloated with hundreds of redundant detached variants. Component properties reduce variant counts by up to 80% while maximizing team efficiency.
lessons.what_learner_does: Engineer an atomic button component featuring 4 visual variants (Primary, Secondary, Ghost, Danger), 5 interactive states, boolean icon toggles, and instance swap properties.
lessons.expected_outcome: A unified master component with clean property controls published in an organized Figma component library.

The Speed Graph Editor: Reading velocity curves, creating exponential deceleration, and snapping pop-ins

lessons.what_learner_does: Animate a bouncing ball morphing into a geometric square and star; adjust velocity curves in the Speed Graph until the bounce demonstrates convincing squash, stretch, and momentum.

Character Reference (--cref) and object consistency: Preserving facial features, wardrobe, and custom product silhouettes
